title: Hooke's Law and Elasticity
short_intro: Hooke's law states that within the elastic limit, the stress developed in a body is directly proportional to the strain produced. For a simple spring, it establishes a linear relation between restoring force and displacement from equilibrium.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Definition of stress, strain, elastic limit, Young's modulus, bulk modulus, modulus of rigidity, and spring constant under simple one-dimensional loading.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Energy stored in stretched strings and springs, tensor treatment of elasticity for complex deformations, interrelations between elastic constants, and dynamic behavior involving oscillations under central/restoring forces.

concept_notes.heading: Fundamentals of Hooke's Law
bullets: States that extension (or compression) x is directly proportional to the applied load F within the proportional limit.
Mathematically expressed as F = -kx, where k is the stiffness constant or spring constant.
The negative sign indicates that the restoring force acts in the direction opposite to the displacement.

concept_notes.heading: Stress-Strain Relationship
bullets: Normal stress (sigma) is defined as restoring force per unit area, measured in N/m² or Pascal.
Longitudinal strain (epsilon) is the fractional change in length (Δl / l).
Within elastic limits, Hooke's law is written as Stress = E × Strain, where E is the relevant modulus of elasticity.

concept_notes.heading: Elastic Moduli
bullets: Young's modulus (Y) relates longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain for solid wires and rods.
Bulk modulus (B) relates hydrostatic pressure to volumetric strain, applicable to fluids and solids alike.
Modulus of rigidity (η) relates shearing stress to shearing strain, governing shape deformation.

concept_notes.heading: Energy Stored in an Elastic Medium
bullets: Work done in stretching an elastic spring is stored as potential energy within the material.
Elastic potential energy density is proportional to the square of the strain multiplied by the elastic modulus.
Total potential energy U = 1/2 kx² for a linearly elastic spring.

derivations.title: Potential Energy of a Stretched Spring
derivations.conditions: Spring obeys Hooke's law up to extension x
steps: Consider an external force F_ext = kx required to stretch a spring slowly by an infinitesimal displacement dx.
The elemental work done dW is given by dW = F_{ext} dx = kx dx.
Integrate the work done from zero extension to a final extension x: W = \int_{0}^{x} kx dx = \frac{1}{2}kx^2.
By conservation of energy, this work appears as elastic potential energy U.

derivations.title: Work Done in Stretching a Wire
derivations.conditions: Wire of initial length L and cross-sectional area A stretched by length ΔL
steps: From Hooke's law, tension T in the wire for an elongation l is given by T = \frac{YA}{L} l.
The small work done to further elongate the wire by dl is dW = T dl = \frac{YA}{L} l dl.
Integrating from l = 0 to l = \Delta L gives W = \int_{0}^{\Delta L} \frac{YA}{L} l dl = \frac{YA}{2L} (\Delta L)^2.
Expressing in terms of stress and strain: W = \frac{1}{2} \times (Stress) \times (Strain) \times (Volume).

graphs_and_experiments.title: Stress-Strain Curve for a Ductile Metal
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A graph with Strain on the x-axis and Stress on the y-axis showing proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Region up to proportional limit follows Hooke's law. Beyond yield point, permanent plastic deformation occurs.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Direct questions identifying yield strength, breaking stress, and regions of permanent set.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Load vs. Elongation Graph for a Spring
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A straight line passing through the origin with Load (F) on y-axis and Elongation (x) on x-axis.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The slope of the straight line directly yields the spring constant k.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Numerical data interpretation to compute stored potential energy or stiffness.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Searle's Apparatus Experiment Setup
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Two parallel wires (experimental and reference) suspended from a rigid support, carrying a spirit level and micrometer screw gauge.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Used to determine Young's modulus of a wire by precisely measuring elongation against added mass while compensating for thermal expansion.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Questions on least count, error propagation, and formula identification for Y.

solved_numericals.question: A spring of force constant 200 N/m is compressed by 5 cm. Calculate the elastic potential energy stored in the spring.
solution_steps: Identify given values: k = 200 N/m, x = 5 cm = 0.05 m.
Apply the formula for potential energy: U = 1/2 kx².

solved_numericals.question: A steel wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 mm² is suspended vertically. When a mass of 10 kg is attached to its lower end, find the elongation produced. (Given Y_steel = 2 × 10^{11} N/m², g = 9.8 m/s²)
solution_steps: Identify parameters: L = 2 m, A = 1 mm² = 10^{-6} m², M = 10 kg, g = 9.8 m/s², Y = 2 × 10^{11} N/m².
Rearrange Young's modulus formula for elongation: ΔL = FL / (YA).

solved_numericals.question: Two identical springs of spring constant k are connected in parallel and then in series. Find the ratio of their effective spring constants (k_{parallel} / k_{series}).
solution_steps: For springs in parallel: k_{parallel} = k + k = 2k.
For springs in series: 1 / k_{series} = 1/k + 1/k = 2/k, so k_{series} = k / 2.

assumptions_and_limitations: Hooke's law is an empirical approximation valid only within the proportional (elastic) limit of a material.
Assumes homogeneous, isotropic materials when defining macroscopic elastic constants like Young's and Bulk moduli.
Fails under large deformations where plastic flow, permanent set, or material rupture occurs.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Hooke's law is a universal law applicable to all materials under any load.
common_misconceptions.correct: Hooke's law holds true only up to the proportional limit for elastic deformations.
common_misconceptions.why: Beyond the elastic limit, stress is no longer proportional to strain, and permanent deformation ensues.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Cutting a spring in half halves its spring constant.
common_misconceptions.correct: Cutting a spring into half doubles its spring constant.
common_misconceptions.why: Spring constant is inversely proportional to its length (k ∝ 1/L); shorter springs are stiffer.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Modulus of elasticity has dimensions of force.
common_misconceptions.correct: Modulus of elasticity has dimensions of pressure or stress (ML^{-1}T^{-2}).
common_misconceptions.why: It is the ratio of stress to dimensionless strain.

quick_revision: Hooke's law: F = -kx or Stress = E × Strain.
Young's modulus governs longitudinal strain, Bulk modulus governs volumetric strain, and Rigidity modulus governs shear.
Elastic potential energy stored in a spring is U = 1/2 kx².
Spring constant in series combination: 1/k_{eq} = sum(1/k_i); in parallel: k_{eq} = sum(k_i).
